evidence.note: Created an explicit task ledger via TaskCreate, one task per subsystem (HTTP core, DB/broadcast, routes, WS, IRC, SPA, start.sh), establishing an upfront map of the entire feature surface.
Continuously flipped task status in_progress→completed as each subsystem was built and verified, maintaining a live done-vs-remaining picture at subsystem granularity.

Systematic verification sweep covering nearly every contract family — threads/reactions/mentions/slash/search, DMs/files/pins/roles/invitations/groups, invite-only+guest perms, profile validation/413/404/401, resume mid-point, IRC nick collision, UI testids — so no whole subsystem (IRC, search, groups, read-state) was silently dropped.
Debug loops (hub-kill test patch, UI assertion fix, token arg fix) were each closed in a single pass; no repeated re-debugging of the same failure, so no circular/thrashing state emerged.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit, continuously-updated task ledger at subsystem granularity and drove a comprehensive verification sweep that cross-checked essentially every contract family in the spec, catching omissions before finishing — squarely the level-8 behavior of an explicit done/partial/failing status used to decide what to touch next. It does not reach 10 because the tracked ledger is coarse (subsystem-level rather than a precise per-contract map) and thrashing detection was never exercised, since debug loops resolved in one pass rather than spiraling.
